requirements.accept: Actual populated v7->v8 upgrade preserves every earlier row, migration hash, issued payload and named native graph. Repeated upgrade and failed upgrade have explicit atomic outcomes.

Explicit correction declarations connect only issued C065 EvidenceReference versions of the same artifact. One immutable parent per child, multiple branches, no self/cycle/cross-artifact edge; plain issuance adds no correction.

Correction and decision rows preserve their own actor attribution, reason, documentary source/locator, interpretation, recorded UTC and database-assigned sequence independently of immutable endpoint sources. Update/delete/replace fail.

Selection queries require exact artifact, named application context and as_of_sequence. A context selects an explicit issued version, not the newest timestamp, label, branch or truth. Missing selection yields NO_SELECTION; CLEAR removes a context's selected pointer without deleting history.

Append-only WITHDRAW notices are context-specific documentary decisions about an exact issued version. At/after withdrawal an already selected version yields WITHDRAWN with null selected_version, never fallback. Earlier as-of queries and all graphs/edges/sources remain unchanged.

Keep C065/C066, R-68/RX-021 and version/item/target pins in their original named graphs. C066 remains contextual. Correction/withdrawal/selection are supplementary metadata, with no native authority/correction/occurrence predicate or inferred independent corroboration.

Reject unknown/unissued/mismatched targets, missing context/provenance and invalid event envelopes without partial writes. Preserve raw unknown identities. Validate current schema/FKs/configuration and refuse v8 with an old exact-schema reader. Execute nested rollback and backup/reopen/dump recovery.

Reconcile all 306 native dispositions and every ELC requirement to fixed inputs, expected/observed SQL/native outcomes, exact code/component and retained claim/limit. Keep 423 historical rows, original source/requirement priorities, eleven WITHHELD admissions and zero independent ratings unchanged.

Use frozen literal expectations independent of the implementation. Deliberately wrong newest-version, missing-context and cross-version-pin mutations must be detected. Software/source accounting never counts as independent semantic ratings.

policy.endpoints: Only the existing issued C065 EvidenceReference family; no arbitrary native assertion, assessment, scenario or source-reference lifecycle is implemented by this new slice. Their previous profiles remain available unchanged.
policy.corrections: Immutable explicit child->parent metadata, same artifact and C065 family, acyclic, single parent per child. Query the selected root and declared descendants once, preserving all branches. No automatic new edge from issuing a version. Diagnostic precedence is envelope/provenance, endpoint existence/issuance/family, same-artifact, self/parent/cycle; controls for a later rule satisfy earlier rules.
policy.decisions: SELECT, WITHDRAW and CLEAR are attributed application decisions scoped to (context_id, artifact_id). Context is a supplementary caller policy identifier, not a new native actor, mandate, authorization or authoritative branch.
policy.sequencing: Database assigns a positive append-only ledger sequence atomically. Selection queries require an explicit as_of_sequence high-water mark and include rows <= it. Sequence records local knowledge order; UTC recorded/source-effective times stay distinct and do not establish real-world validity. Timestamp ties cannot choose a winner; sequence is explicit. Deterministic fixture sequences are expected data, not evidence of an actual run. Omitted/negative/noninteger as-of boundaries are INVALID_AS_OF_SEQUENCE. New event/request IDs are unique and cannot replace committed events.
policy.selection: Within a context and as-of bound, the last SELECT/CLEAR decides the pointer. No SELECT means NO_SELECTION. CLEAR means NO_SELECTION. A selected version withdrawn in that context by that bound means WITHDRAWN with selected_version=null and last_selected_version retained. Otherwise SELECTED returns that exact version. Newest issued version, corrections or another context never supply a fallback.
policy.withdrawal: WITHDRAW references an exact existing issued C065 version and remains documentary/application-scoped. It never erases payload, source, correction edge, native graph or another context's decision. A withdrawn version cannot be newly selected in the same context. Reinstatement of an erroneous withdrawal and notice-level correction are deferred; a future reviewed supplement must preserve the original notice rather than mutate it.
policy.provenance: Keep artifact-origin, endpoint-version and correction/decision-source attribution separate. Actor identifiers are documentary attribution, not verified access control or native authority. Mandatory source identity/locator, interpretation and reason are explicit; unconfirmed facts remain unknown/raw. Real-calendar UTC syntax and mandatory attribution fields are validated; invalid/missing values cause no writes.
policy.raw_managed: An unknown artifact/item/target is retained as raw input and cannot receive an issued lifecycle decision. No invented target or organizational case identity.
policy.native_projection: Reuse the four literal EQR 0.6.0 named-graph oracles unchanged. New correction/decision rows contribute no new native triples. Old/new version graphs remain distinct; no historical union.
policy.migration: Additive migration 8 over an actually populated, validated v7 source; do not change migration 1..7 files or pre-existing rows. Preserve raw/managed separation and all prior schema/payload/hash audits. Old exact-schema readers reject v8.
policy.missingness: Absent source/identity/context/selection is not zero, false, endorsement, nonexistence or truth. Unknown policy context produces NO_SELECTION; omitted context is INVALID_CONTEXT.
out_of_scope: Global authority, truth, endorsement or independent corroboration
New model/ORSD semantics or independent scientific validation
policy.implementation_change_control: If actual schema/API design cannot satisfy these fixed expectations, record a reasoned contract/oracle amendment in a new commit before implementation continues; never replace expected answers with observed output.
